A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same mask-permutation research. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10/100 and ImageNet experiments, including sparse-training accuracy, connectivity, ensemble diversity and early-matching results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: IMP mask construction, activation matching, mask permutation, weight rewinding and sparse training are unchanged. Appendix B explains early matching more explicitly, but that procedure already appears in v1's Table 15.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and ImageNet classification tasks. No dataset, domain or distinct testing scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The benchmark comparisons retain LTH, naive mask reuse and dense references. Table 1 retains the same IMP, LTH, permuted and naive ensemble comparisons; the changed PyTorch citation introduces no evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix C changes the stated source mask/initialization from M0,w0 to M1,w1 while retaining w1–w5 for permuted ensemble members. Read literally, the revised description now includes the source initialization among those members. This is a limited change to the reported setup; no rerun is established. Other training budgets, metrics, preprocessing and rewind settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The REPAIR comparison, connectivity visualizations, width and sparsity analyses, ensemble-diversity study and early-matching experiment are retained. Appendix B's expanded explanation adds no analysis or result beyond the existing Table 15.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three-run averaging for CIFAR rewind experiments and five runs/seeds for ensemble analyses, with the same ± reporting. Appendix C corrects a six-label mask list to five labels while retaining the explicitly stated five-seed count.

E6.justification: Figure 7 changes the dense ImageNet Top-5 reference from 91.2% to 93.0% and adjusts several sparse-model points to agree with the unchanged Table 10. For example, naive accuracy at 80% sparsity and rewind 25 changes from 88.0% to 88.1%. Result-table values and the principal rankings remain unchanged; these revisions do not establish new performance gains.

T1.justification: The activation-matching formulation, weight-permutation equations and loss-barrier definition in Equations 1–3 are unchanged. Neither version adds a formal theorem or proof; Appendix B's added notation restates the existing early-matching procedure.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same central claims: basin alignment improves mask transfer, permuted models provide greater functional diversity than LTH, and correcting variance collapse reveals dense–sparse connectivity. The abstract's addition concerns code access.

C2.justification: The basin-mismatch interpretation, explanations involving matching accuracy and model width, ImageNet and VGG11 caveats, and computational and hardware limitations remain. The early-matching rewrite retains the existing interpretation that earlier alignment can reduce computational cost.

D1.justification: v2 adds an abstract statement that the codebase is public and supplies a repository hyperlink; v1 provides no corresponding code-access information. Architecture, augmentation, optimizer and pruning details in Appendix A and Tables 2–4 remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A.2 replaces the PyTorch examples citation, Contributors (2024), with Paszke et al. (2019), and the bibliography changes accordingly. Appendix B also softens its description of Sharma et al. from early permutation stability to the feasibility of early matching. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 adds an author Contribution Statement, expands Appendix B, revises Appendix C's indexing, removes numbering from the Impact Statement and Acknowledgements, and makes scattered wording and bibliographic edits. The main narrative and section organization remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 7 is redrawn as three wider, vertically stacked panels with revised ticks. Table 1 and Figure 8 are repositioned on the same page, Table 15 is reduced in size, and surrounding material reflows. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: The added code-location information, clearer early-matching explanation and corrections aligning Figure 7's sparse results with Table 10 provide modest practical improvements. The scientific method and evidence remain essentially unchanged. The unexplained dense-reference update and Appendix C's source-initialization labeling leave local reporting ambiguities that limit the gain.
